patterns.title: Bounded measurable real functions are integrable under a finite measure

proof_detail.explanation: Instantiate the existing finite-measure bounded-integrability lemma after identifying the measure, function and actual almost-everywhere bound.
remaining_obligations: Provide the finite-measure instance, almost-everywhere strong measurability and norm bound for the mapped objects.

example.context:
open MeasureTheory
variable {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
  (f : Ω → ℝ) (C : ℝ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ)
  (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ C)

limitations: A bounded integrand alone does not give integrability under an infinite measure.
patterns.application_template:
refine (show MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure {{measure}} →
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable {{integrand}} {{measure}} →
    (∀ᵐ x ∂{{measure}}, ‖{{integrand}} x‖ ≤ {{uniform_bound}}) →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable {{integrand}} {{measure}} from by
  intro hfinite hmeas hbound
  letI := hfinite
  exact MeasureTheory.Integrable.of_bound hmeas {{uniform_bound}} hbound) ?_ ?_ ?_
all_goals first | assumption | skip

patterns.title: An eventual real upper bound passes to an existing limit

conditions.name: eventual_bound
conditions.lean_type: ∀ᶠ n in atTop, a n ≤ B

proof_detail.explanation: Supply the proved limit and the eventual inequality to le_of_tendsto. The inequality does not establish existence of the limit.
remaining_obligations: Identify the existing convergence theorem and establish the eventual inequality with the same filter and scalar values.

example.context:
open Filter
open scoped Topology
variable (a : ℕ → ℝ) (L B : ℝ)
  (hlimit : Tendsto a atTop (𝓝 L))
  (hbound : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, a n ≤ B)

limitations: An eventual inequality cannot substitute for the convergence hypothesis.
patterns.application_template:
refine (show Filter.Tendsto {{finite_scale_values}} Filter.atTop (𝓝 {{limit_value}}) →
    (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, {{finite_scale_values}} n ≤ {{upper_bound}}) →
    {{limit_value}} ≤ {{upper_bound}} from by
  intro hlimit hbound
  exact le_of_tendsto hlimit hbound) ?_ ?_
all_goals first | assumption | skip

patterns.title: A nonnegative real defect dominated by a strict contraction vanishes

proof_detail.explanation: If D were positive, multiplying κ < 1 by D would give κD < D, contradicting the supplied contraction. This is finite real arithmetic.
remaining_obligations: Map the actual defect to a finite real scalar and prove its nonnegativity and strict contraction.

example.context: variable (D κ : ℝ) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (hκ : κ < 1) (hcontract : D ≤ κ * D)
example.candidate:
by_contra hne
have hpos : 0 < D := lt_of_le_of_ne hD (Ne.symm hne)
have hstrict := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hκ hpos
nlinarith

proof_detail.provenance: Curated finite-real arithmetic pattern. The project reference uses finite edist when invoking contraction uniqueness; the example below is checked separately by Lean.

limitations: Do not transfer this pattern to ℝ≥0∞ without separately proving that the defect is finite.
patterns.application_template:
refine (show ∀ (D κ : ℝ), 0 ≤ D → κ < 1 → D ≤ κ * D → D = 0 from by
  intro D κ hD hκ hcontract
  by_contra hne
  have hpos : 0 < D := lt_of_le_of_ne hD (Ne.symm hne)
  have hstrict := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hκ hpos
  nlinarith) {{defect}} {{contraction_factor}} ?_ ?_ ?_
all_goals first | assumption | skip

patterns.title: Infinity prevents transferring finite-real contraction reasoning to ENNReal

proof_detail.explanation: The infinite defect satisfies D ≤ (1/2)D and remains nonzero. The real-valued contraction pattern therefore requires a genuine finiteness argument before conversion to real scalars.
remaining_obligations: For a valid transfer, prove D ≠ ⊤ before using finite real arithmetic; otherwise retain the counterexample.

invalid_transfer.candidate:
refine (show ∀ (D κ : ℝ), 0 ≤ D → κ < 1 → D ≤ κ * D → D = 0 from by
  intro D κ hD hκ hcontract
  by_contra hne
  have hpos : 0 < D := lt_of_le_of_ne hD (Ne.symm hne)
  have hstrict := mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hκ hpos
  nlinarith) (⊤ : ℝ≥0∞) (1 / 2 : ℝ≥0∞) ?_ ?_ ?_
all_goals first | assumption | skip

limitations: This certified counterexample rejects a transfer rule; it does not refute a finite-real theorem.
